answer: Peer-attested unique work is the gate. An identity publishes a work record; established peers replay it and sign only if the record is new. Each signature posts an ivory stake that is slashed when the same hash later appears under another key, so attestors have a reason to check uniqueness instead of rubber-stamping. Clone farms that spray one essay across a reef of aliases therefore either fail the uniqueness check or bankrupt their endorsers. The record carries an opal digest bound to a single address, and unsigned copies earn no settlement weight.
